source: Raw sf.ethereum.type.v2.Block captures (DETAILLEVEL_EXTENDED) from a Pinax Firehose endpoint, one block per request, fetched on 2026-10-17 for the v0.7.4 investigation. A case with a provenance field is an earlier capture described there.
extraction: Cut at the protobuf wire level by a scratch script kept outside the repository: the listed transaction_traces (Block field 10) keep their exact bytes, as does every other top-level field (header, hash, number, system calls and block-level records), in the original order. No field edits.
rows: Every row map_events emits for the fixture, by contract and holder, as v0.7.4 gives it. Each fixture row was checked offline to equal the row v0.7.4 gives for the same pair on the full source block (except for the earlier captures, whose full blocks are not kept); added_since_v073 lists the pairs v0.7.3 does not emit on the fixture.
rpc_era: Read-only, 2026-10-17: the RPC-era database (mainnet:, bsc: or polygon:evm-balances@v0.3.3), table historical_erc20_balances_state, interval_min = 1. For each fixture row, the 1-minute bar of the block's minute is read at the block when the bar starts (open) or ends (close) there; holders without such a bar are not listed. A case's rpc_era.method, where present, replaces this method.
keyed: A calls entry's keyed, where present, states whether the call or its DELEGATECALL members record a verified 64-byte preimage of pad(input[16..36]) in either key order (pad(holder) || slot or slot || pad(holder)), so whether v0.7.4 reads it as keyed.

cases.selection: the bot transaction 1; the block's other WBNB transactions, 12 (reverted), 16, 20 and 47, are omitted, and none of their WBNB logs names a holder of the fixture's rows
cases.demonstrates: on a Block.ver 3 producer, which never cuts call data, a bot transaction CALLs WBNB balanceOf four times with 68-byte keyed inputs (calls 2, 3, 28 and 29); v0.7.3 dropped WBNB for the block, v0.7.4 reads them

cases.selection: every WETH transaction with one call, and transaction 27
cases.demonstrates: tx 27 (Block.ver 3) STATICCALLs WETH balanceOf(0xed777775...) twice with 64-byte inputs (calls 2 and 15); v0.7.3 dropped WETH for the block, v0.7.4 reads them

cases.selection: transaction 50 and the first ten USDT transactions with one call whose holders appear in no other USDT transaction of the block
cases.demonstrates: tx 50 (Block.ver 4) STATICCALLs USDT balanceOf with a 28-byte input (call 2), which TetherToken (solc 0.4.18) answers with balanceOf(0) of the zero-extended argument; v0.7.3 dropped USDT for the block, v0.7.4 reads it only to veto

cases.selection: every USDT transaction with one call, and the bot transaction 97
cases.demonstrates: a bot transaction (tx 97, Block.ver 5) CALLs balanceOf(0x1dd00b11...) of USDT, USDC and WETH with 68-byte inputs (pad(holder) and a leftover word of its transfer buffer) that return the stored word; v0.7.3 dropped all three tokens for the block on the input length, v0.7.4 reads each as balanceOf(input[16..36]). The USDT read (call 38) is keyed in its own frame, and the USDC read (call 9) through its DELEGATECALL to the FiatToken implementation (call 10, which records pad(holder) || 9)

cases.selection: every USDC transaction with at most two calls (a proxied transfer), and the bot transaction 166
cases.demonstrates: tx 166 (Block.ver 5) CALLs USDC balanceOf(0x52852bd8...) with a 68-byte input (call 96), keyed through its DELEGATECALL to the FiatToken implementation (call 97, which records pad(holder) || 9), returning the stored 5,769,348, and WETH balanceOf with a 68-byte input keyed in its own frame (call 91); v0.7.3 dropped both tokens for the block, v0.7.4 reads both and keeps their rows; since C6 the block's FXN (a CurveDAOToken fork, Vyper 0.3.1) rows are inferred too

cases.selection: transaction 18 only, as captured in 2026-09
cases.demonstrates: deposit() five frames deep, called by the storage address 0x278d858f... (tx 18 call 13, Block.ver 5) with exactly the wad and no call; in the one-transaction capture WBNB has no Transfer, so the frame votes the credit and the holder gets its word

rpc_era.note: Not confirmed at the block, read-only, 2026-10-17: the RPC era has no 1-minute bar there; its observations before (block 122,287,736: 986695725389579487777) and after (block 122,288,121: 981759524013973611004) bracket it. In the capture, the token's own balanceOf of the holder traced after the deposit in the same transaction (call 19) returns the row. The full block is not kept, so later transactions of the block are not reflected.

cases.selection: the whole block (its only transaction is the state sync)
cases.demonstrates: the Polygon Block.ver 3 state-sync transaction (tx 0, ordinals 1 to 57) commits ten events; each depth-1 commitState call restarts the ordinals at 4 or 5. Four bridge deposits mint PoS WETH in subtrees 0, 5, 8 and 9, whose total-supply writes fall at ordinals 17, 15, 15 and 15. By ordinal they tie and v0.7.3 dropped WETH; in call order they chain and the four holders get rows

rpc_era.method: Indirect, read-only, 2026-10-17: polygon:evm-balances@v0.3.3 has no 1-minute bar at these blocks for the holders the state sync names, so each value is the holder's nearest RPC-era observation before the block (historical_erc20_balances_state) plus the net of its transfer, deposit and withdrawal rows in between (polygon:evm-transfers@v0.3.3, summed in ClickHouse), checked again against the nearest observation after the block. Only rows of contracts that the state-sync transaction writes are listed.

cases.selection: every WPOL transaction: 509, 607, 652 and the state sync 662
cases.demonstrates: the Polygon Block.ver 3 state-sync transaction (tx 662, ordinals 10,389 to 10,585) commits five events. In subtrees 0 and 4, deposits of the bridged token 0x712f0cf3... are swapped to POL through the WPOL pool 0x3d4cc8a6..., whose WPOL word is written at ordinal 10,534 in subtree 0 and 10,532 in subtree 4: by ordinal the writes run backwards and v0.7.3 dropped WPOL and 0x712f0cf3...; in call order they chain. The balanceOf calls inside the transaction compare with the word call order gives, so 0x1fdeaf93... keeps its three rows

cases.selection: every scrvUSD transaction (only the report transaction 178)
cases.demonstrates: a report of scrvUSD, a Yearn v3 VaultV3 behind an EIP-1167 proxy (implementation 0xd8063123..., Vyper 0.3.7): the vault's DELEGATECALL frame (tx 178 call 51) emits Transfer(0, vault, 3615774490983119344) and writes the vault's own word under HashMap slot 18, preimage slot || pad(vault), to 5480155112664263237347 at ordinal 9603. VaultV3 computes balanceOf(self) as that word less the shares still unlocking, so under the Vyper base the vault never gets a row of its own; no balanceOf(vault) follows the write (right after a report the word equals the RPC era, which it later does not). crvUSD (Vyper 0.3.7, slot 1) gets its two rows; v0.7.3 read neither token's preimages

setcode_transactions.source: Arbitrum One Firehose (Pinax), fetched 2026-10-17 with firecore tools firehose-client -o bytes --bytes-encoding base64, and -o json for the same block hash. Copied byte for byte from native v0.7.9's fixtures (native/balances/tests/fixtures/, provenance arbitrum-setcode-v079.json).
setcode_transactions.extraction: Sliced the selected transaction's TransactionTrace bytes (Block field 10) out of the encoded Extended block without decoding or editing them. No RPC was used.
setcode_transactions.limits: Arbitrum One, Block.ver 3, whose root calls record begin_ordinal 0. Five failed SetCode transactions whose sender authorizes itself with the transaction's own nonce, an authorization that cannot apply and that the producer leaves unmarked; ERC-20 v0.7.3 and native v0.7.8 refuse their blocks. Not a producer matrix.
setcode_transactions.rows: A failed transaction persists no storage write or log, so no slice gives an ERC-20 row: run gives none for each slice alone, where v0.7.3 refused it.
